title: Lights — Solid State Lighting Conversion for Cabins at the Extended Premium Layout

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Variant of the solid state lighting conversion for aircraft already rebuilt to the extended premium layout, where the ceiling channel geometry differs and a transition piece is needed at every cabin boundary.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft rebuilt to the extended premium layout have a ceiling channel that changes section at each cabin boundary, because the layout moved the boundaries away from the original monument positions. The standard conversion extrusion does not follow that section and cannot be clipped in across a boundary. Operators with these aircraft need the same tube obsolescence answer as everybody else, and this variant gives it to them without a further cabin rebuild.
sections.description: The conversion is as the standard Service Bulletin except at the cabin boundaries, where a transition piece bridges the change of channel section and carries the strip through without a break in the addressing. The obsolete galley insert D3320009917460 is removed as before, the partition NY719919-92 is retained, and bolts LN983579-8C secure both the extrusion and the transition pieces. The obsolete panel RO886925-91 is not fitted on this layout and no action is needed against it.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on ground power and isolate the cabin lighting distribution. Survey the cabin and record the position of every channel section change against the layout drawing. Remove the ceiling and wall panels along the run to be converted. Remove the fluorescent tubes and their ballasts and remove the obsolete galley insert D3320009917460. Remove the partition NY719919-92 and store it. Install the extrusion in each straight run, securing it with bolts LN983579-8C. Fit a transition piece at every recorded section change and check that the strip seats without preload. Clip the strips in and connect them front to rear, keeping the addressing continuous across each transition. Refit the partition and the ceiling and wall panels. Energise the cabin, load the addressing and do the lighting installation check of AMM-T-33-20-11-400-002-A. Confirm that no addressing gap exists at any boundary. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft from MSN T00100 to MSN T00213 that have been rebuilt to the extended premium layout. MSN T00164 is excluded. Aircraft in the original layout are covered by the standard conversion Service Bulletin, and an aircraft must not be treated under both.
sections.material_note: Kit K3320-1051-01 covers one main deck and includes the transition pieces, quantity depending on the layout variant declared at order. Kit lead time is thirty-four weeks. Removed tubes are hazardous waste and are disposed of locally.

type_data.compliance_time: At operator convenience, normally at a cabin refresh.

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Variant of the solid state lighting conversion for aircraft already rebuilt to the extended premium layout, where the ceiling channel geometry differs, a transition piece is needed at every cabin boundary, and the convertible run is bounded by frame station at its aft end.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft rebuilt to the extended premium layout have a ceiling channel that changes section at each cabin boundary, because the layout moved the boundaries away from the original monument positions. The standard conversion extrusion does not follow that section and cannot be clipped in across a boundary. Operators with these aircraft need the same tube obsolescence answer as everybody else, and this variant gives it to them without a further cabin rebuild.
sections.description: The conversion is as the standard Service Bulletin except at the cabin boundaries, where a transition piece bridges the change of channel section and carries the strip through without a break in the addressing. The obsolete galley insert D3320009917460 is removed as before, the partition NY719919-92 is retained, and bolts LN983579-8C secure both the extrusion and the transition pieces. The obsolete panel RO886925-91 is not fitted on this layout and no action is needed against it.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on ground power and isolate the cabin lighting distribution. Survey the cabin and record the position of every channel section change against the layout drawing, and record the aft end of the convertible run at frame station C74. Remove the ceiling and wall panels along the run to be converted. Remove the fluorescent tubes and their ballasts and remove the obsolete galley insert D3320009917460. Remove the partition NY719919-92 and store it. Install the extrusion in each straight run, securing it with bolts LN983579-8C. Fit a transition piece at every recorded section change and check that the strip seats without preload. Clip the strips in and connect them front to rear, keeping the addressing continuous across each transition, and terminate the addressing at the C74 boundary with the end-of-run cap so that a later extension can be joined to it. Refit the partition and the ceiling and wall panels. Energise the cabin, load the addressing and do the lighting installation check of AMM-T-33-20-11-400-002-A. Confirm that no addressing gap exists at any boundary. Record the embodiment and record the frame station at which the run was terminated.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft from MSN T00100 to MSN T00213 that have been rebuilt to the extended premium layout. MSN T00164 is excluded. Aircraft in the original layout are covered by the standard conversion Service Bulletin, and an aircraft must not be treated under both. This bulletin converts the run forward of frame station C74, which on the extended premium layout reaches further aft than the original cabin boundary and already takes in the forward part of the upper deck lobby. Work aft of C74 is not covered here and is the only part of the lobby that a further conversion has to address; scoping a lobby extension without reading this boundary duplicates about two thirds of the run on these aircraft.
sections.material_note: Kit K3320-1051-01 covers one main deck and includes the transition pieces, quantity depending on the layout variant declared at order. Kit lead time is thirty-four weeks. Removed tubes are hazardous waste and are disposed of locally.

type_data.compliance_time: At operator convenience, normally at a cabin refresh.

revision_history.reason: Aft boundary of the convertible run stated at frame station C74 and the addressing termination added
